browser.method: A persisted state is seeded (as workspace storage would), the page is reloaded, and the analysis result arrives afterwards, as it does after a restart.

notStarted.note: The view requests the projection for the restored scope once the result exists; nothing starts an analysis.

browser.persistence: The webview wrote a 302-byte versioned state to setState/localStorage containing target, selection, filters, scope, panes, table page, and camera.

unitTests.serializer: Round trip with camera; a different schema version is ignored; pane widths clamp to 140-480/200-720; a local scope without an id becomes root; a malformed camera, filters, and table page are dropped.
unitTests.protocol: viewState maps to stateRestored, carries the camera, and never produces an analyze action.

conclusions.hideAndReturn: restore is verified for the whole acceptance list (target, selection, filter state, camera) in the browser fixture.
conclusions.noSilentRun: No analysis state is persisted, so a restore cannot start Semantic or the generator; the fixture shows zero analyze requests.
conclusions.crashSafety: Old schema versions and narrow widths are handled by the version guard and clamps (unit-tested).
conclusions.retainContextWhenHidden: Now false: the restore covers the recreated webview.

notVerifiedHere: Real VS Code hide/show, window reload, and workspace-storage round trips (SD-027).
Auto-refresh is not implemented (default OFF by design); debounce and request coalescing remain for a later change.
